creator: Alexander Terp
description:
`*rest str` already collects the rest verbatim, flags included, so the `**rest` arg kind this card was cut for doesn't need building. Neither does the argv-safe interpolation half: list-form commands (`$["claude"] + rest`) shipped since, and carry `hello world`, `a$b`, `semi;colon` and `*` through untouched.

For a pure passthrough that is already enough. `dev` (`~/src/scripts/bin/dev`) can drop `@enable_args_block = 0` and its `get_args()[1:].join(" ")` quoting bug today, for:

```
---
@enable_global_options = 0
---
args:
    *rest str
```

Checked against HEAD: `-r --continue`, `-p 'do it' -r`, `up -r`, `-h`, `--help`, `-q`, `-i` and the empty case all reach `rest` intact.

What still fails is the mixed wrapper - own flags plus passthrough - which is what `ct` (1103 runs) is. Two causes, only one of them a bug.

Every arg is both a flag and a positional (`core/args.go:23-45`), so `ct`'s own `model` and its `*rest` compete for untagged tokens and `model` is always first in line. Separately, rad cannot know the child's grammar: in `ct -p "do it"`, whether `do it` is `-p`'s value or `ct`'s own positional is unanswerable from rad's side.

The first cause has a location. `ra_cmd_parse.go:1313-1373` guards the five slice branches with `if src == posUnknownFlagToken && !f.Variadic { continue }`; the five scalar branches above them (1258-1307) have no such guard, so a scalar positional swallows flag-shaped tokens. Registering `ct`'s shape against ra directly:

```
--continue -p x       ->  model="--continue"  rest=["-p" "x"]
-r --continue -m 2    ->  model="2"           rest=["--continue"]
-P -r                 ->  model="-r"          rest=[]
```

The middle one loses `-r` with no error at all: it binds to `model` positionally, then `-m 2` overwrites it.

Adding the guard to the scalar branches fixes those three. `--continue -p x` still puts `x` on `model`, and no parser change reaches that - it is the second cause. Declaring `ct`'s own args flag-only does reach it, because a wrapper owning no positional has nothing left competing for bare tokens. ra already has `SetFlagOnly`; rad only sets it for script args under subcommands (`core/runner.go:636`), so an args block has no way to ask for it. That syntax is the feature here; everything else on this card is repair.

One case survives both: `-r -P --continue` errors, because collection stops at a known flag and never reopens (`findNextUnassignedVariadicPositional:624` skips anything configured; `collectPositionalIntoSlice:1395` refuses once `sawFlag`). `--` already has an explicit reopen rule at `ra_cmd_parse.go:1405`, so extending it to flag-shaped tokens is one line - scoped to variadics, so `str[]` keeps the non-resumption that multi-section parsing depends on.

With those three ra edits plus flag-only, all six shapes parse correctly (verified on a patched copy). ra's suite then has exactly one failure, `Test_VariadicUnknownFlags_KnownFlagStopsCollection`, which asserts the behavior being changed - a decision to make, not a regression to chase.

`ct` still can't move over completely afterwards: its `-m` and `-o` take an optional value, which is `optional-value-flags`. `reject-dash-prefixed` is done but covered flag values only; the positional door it left open is what this card closes.

Separable, and unrelated to the parsing work: an uncaught `$` failure exits 1 rather than the child's code. `core/shell.go:116` puts the code in the error's message only, and `RadErrorExit` (`core/printer.go:267`) hardcodes 1. Propagating already works, streaming output and all:

```
code = $`echo streaming; exit 42` catch:
    exit(code)
```

So this is a default to change, not a mechanism to build.
title: Add flag-only args, so wrappers can use the args block
